verdicts.title: plans.py tier parity: validate iter_tuples count; align the struct-tier endian gate with the swap predicate
verdicts.issues: Re-ran on my own patched copy: over-count raises the exact ValueError on both a struct-tier and a shiftmask-tier plan; count=None/exact unchanged; the big-endian-parent/little-child record of byte-order-agnostic leaves (4-byte Buffer + u8s) now compiles to tier 'struct' with output byte-identical to the audit's shiftmask bytes (b'ABCD\x07\x09' == 414243440709) and round-trips; a little-u16-in-big record still demotes and swaps (b'\x02\x01'). Composes correctly with the AMENDED plans-1 guard: the iter_tuples avail check fires before any slice, so the shiftmask over-count gets this clearer message instead of plans-1's incidental 'expected N bytes, got 0', and the struct tier's silent truncation (finding-26 residue plans-1's reviewer flagged) is genuinely fixed - the uniform-raise claim holds. Floats correctly stay strict (they cannot even reach shiftmask: Plan.__init__ raises PlanCompileError for kind 'f' there). NITS: (a) the compiler already normalizes directly-declared kind-'b' field endian to the record's (plans.py ~451-455 'never force the shiftmask tier on their account'), so the gate's kind=='b' clause only matters for nested-Struct leaves (copied verbatim with child endian) and hand-built Plans - worth stating; (b) with offset beyond the buffer, avail goes negative and the message reads 'only -3 whole records' - raising is right, wording odd; (c) PRE-EXISTING: avail counts len(view) items, not bytes, for itemsize>1 memoryviews - consistent with iter_tuples' existing item-based slicing but diverges from AMENDED plans-1's nbytes-counting unpack_tuple guard on that exotic input.

verdicts.title: Make 1-bit sign-magnitude (and ones'-complement) SInt constructible: handle the zero-width magnitude field
verdicts.issues: Re-ran their probes plus boundary adversarials on my patched copy: SInt1(0) constructs in both formats with 1-bit .bits; to_bitstring(0, bit_length=1, signed_magnitude) == '0'; decode '1' == 0 (minus zero) in both formats; encode of -1/1 at n_bits=1 correctly still rejected by the existing range guards (abs(n) > 2**0-1); two's-complement '1' still -1; wider widths bit-identical ('1010' -> -2 sm / -5 oc). Claim that only the signed_magnitude path passes width 0 verified by reading all four callers of unsigned_int_to_bitstring (entry path requires bit_length >= 1; ones_complement passes full width). Suite 854/854. No issues.

verdicts.issues: Re-ran their probes plus boundaries: (-200,8)/(300,8)/(128,8) raise; -128/127/-1 at 8 bits and default-width tc(-5) unchanged; n_bits=1 boundary correct (0->'0', -1->'1', 1 raises). ISSUE (composition claim inaccurate): the after-text does NOT byte-identically embed aggregate-utils-5's accepted docstring as claimed - it rewrites it: accepted 'n_bits (int): The bit width for the two's complement representation.' became 'n_bits (int, optional): The bit width for the two's complement\n representation.' (re-wrapped, type annotation changed) and the accepted Returns line 'str: A string of the number's two's-complement bits.' is REPLACED by 'str: A string of exactly ``n_bits`` binary digits.'. The combined form is self-consistent and strictly more precise, so applying it as the final form works - but the maintainer should know it supersedes, not embeds, aggregate-utils-5's accepted wording (drift, not byte-identical embed).

verdicts.title: Oracle sync: give to_bytes_aggregate the same multi-char-str carve-out as to_bits_aggregate (required once pytypes-3 lands); drop the commented scaffolding
verdicts.issues: RESOLVED by orchestrator revision: the Rec('ABC', 5) regression vs the pytypes-3 world is now disclosed in risks, and the decision reframed as a three-option string policy choice (strict / carve-out / carve-out + declared-width check, with (c) recommended). Original issue: REPRODUCED THE HEADLINE CLAIMS, all true: on a pristine copy + pytypes-3 alone, to_bytes_aggregate('hi') hard-breaks (ValueError 'encodes to 2 UTF-8 bytes') through both the public wrapper and the oracle - the severity upgrade and land-with-or-before-pytypes-3 pairing are justified; adding the carve-out restores b'hi' via both entry points, bytes(to_bits_aggregate('hi')) == b'hi', and the disclosed little-endian delta is exactly as stated (b'ih' -> b'hi'); full suite 854/854 in the pt3+carve world (parity oracle included); scaffolding deletion is comment-only and the line ranges are verbatim-correct; the oracle-procedure framing is sound (single-copy edit verified - the public wrapper short-circuits only plan-eligible dataclasses and delegates every str to the oracle; frozen-oracle treated as coordination procedure per house rule). DUAL-DIVERGENCE ANSWER: the carve-out RESOLVES pytypes-3's flagged bits/bytes divergence for bare multi-char strings (both paths now per-char) - it does not sit beside it. WHY ok=false - UNDISCLOSED REGRESSION vs the accepted pytypes-3 baseline: to_bytes_aggregate(Rec('ABC', 5)) reverts from pytypes-3's advertised loud ValueError-at-serialize (literally one of pytypes-3's suggested tests: 'pytest.raises(ValueError): to_bytes_aggregate(Rec(\'ABC\', 5)) (fails loudly at serialize time now)') back to silently emitting b'ABC\x00\x00\x00\x05' that fails round-trip far from cause - empirically confirmed on the pt3+carve copy. That is the exact silent-corruption shape pytypes-3's problem statement targeted, now symmetric on both paths. The risks section's 'it is the one input whose bytes change' is only true against the pristine baseline, not against the pytypes-3 world this solution says it must pair with; if pytypes-3's tests land as written, this carve-out breaks one of them. The fix direction is defensible (per-char consistency, matching pytypes-3's own 'char semantics' reasoning and its open decision question), but the Rec-multi-char revert and the pytypes-3 test conflict must be disclosed and decided (accept revert + amend pytypes-3's test, or keep the loud failure for dataclass fields) before landing.

verdicts.title: ConversionInfo.to_bytes/from_bytes: take endianness and mirror the module functions exactly
verdicts.issues: Applied on top of pytypes-1 (its before matches pytypes-1's accepted after) and re-ran the parity loop: for int(pos/neg)/float/bool/str-char x big/little, info.to_bytes(v,e) == pytype_to_bytes(v,e) and info.from_bytes(b,e) == bytes_to_pytype(b,t,e). The bytes-vs-.to_bytes() alignment claim is empirically true: bytes(info.to_bits(True)) == b'\x80' while .to_bytes() == b'\x01' == pytype_to_bytes(True), so the amendment is a real behavioral fix to pytypes-1's spelling for the 1-bit bool codec, not just style. Literal is already imported in pytypes.py. The bitvector-behavior-7 interaction reasoning holds structurally: both the method and the module function route through BitVector.to_bytes(), so parity survives behavior-7's semantics change regardless (and registered codecs are 1-bit/whole-byte anyway). Suite 854/854. No substantive issues; the amendment supersedes pytypes-1's docstring wording for the two methods, which is coherent.

verdicts.title: Broad `except Exception` triage: narrow the plan-compile probe, document the byte-convertibility probe, keep the re-raisers
verdicts.issues: The EDIT is verified safe: fallback survives for non-plannable dataclasses (bare-list field -> _get_record_plan is None), plannable records still plan and round-trip, the ByteConvertible probe still swallows a raising __bytes__, suite 854/854. ISSUE (rationale factually wrong, though the change still works): the claim that plans.py 'funnels every compile-time failure into PlanCompileError (it wraps foreign exceptions at plans.py:448 and 470)' is false on two counts - those sites catch PlanCompileError and re-raise PlanCompileError with context (no foreign-exception wrapping), and they live in compile_plan, a function _get_record_plan never calls. _get_record_plan calls compile_legacy_record_plan, whose designed 'not plannable' channel is RETURNING None (it never raises PlanCompileError anywhere in its body), so the narrowed 'except PlanCompileError' is in practice dead code and the fallback works entirely through the None channel. The behavioral consequence stated (non-PlanCompileError escapes now propagate, e.g. get_type_hints NameError, which the legacy path would raise later anyway - verified the legacy dataclass branches also call resolve_field_types) is correct, so the diff is sound; but the maintainer should not accept the stated mechanism at face value - consider whether keeping the dead except (future-proofing) or dropping the try entirely is the honest form.
